alerts.title: Creatinine recorded only as pasted text
alerts.message: A creatinine result appears only in pasted lab text, so its date is unknown. Check when it was taken and enter it as a dated lab result for a patient on TDF.

alerts.title: NSAID use mentioned while on TDF
alerts.message: NSAID use is mentioned in notes for a patient on TDF. Consider reviewing renal risk and ensuring appropriate monitoring.

alerts.title: Proteinuria mentioned in notes
alerts.message: Proteinuria (or trace protein) is mentioned in notes. Consider follow-up assessment and management per local guidance.

alerts.title: Progressive creatinine rise and reduced eGFR on TDF with NSAID use
alerts.message: Guidelines advise checking creatinine (eGFR) on TDF, and that dehydration or intercurrent illness may worsen renal function. Patient has a steady creatinine rise from 0.9 mg/dL (2020) to 1.4 mg/dL (2026), eGFR now 52 mL/min/1.73m2, and 1+ proteinuria with trace glycosuria. Evidence for TDF nephrotoxicity: sustained trend on TDF for 3 years. Evidence against sole attribution: concurrent ibuprofen 2-3 times weekly for 6 months, which is a recognised cause of renal impairment and interacts with TDF nephrotoxicity risk; non-drug causes such as hypertension or diabetes are not present (BP 118/76, no diabetes), but dehydration from the fatigue history should be assessed.

evidence.recommended_action: Repeat creatinine and eGFR and urinalysis promptly, stop or minimise ibuprofen, assess hydration, and review TDF suitability per guideline renal monitoring thresholds.

alerts.title: Routine DTG viral load monitoring up to date; renal monitoring not documented
alerts.message: Guidelines recommend viral load every 6 months on DTG-based first-line ART; viral load <50 copies/mL is reported and consistent with suppression. However, no renal monitoring plan or clinician assessment is recorded despite the declining eGFR and proteinuria on TDF.

evidence.recommended_action: Document a renal monitoring plan with repeat creatinine/eGFR and urinalysis, and continue 6-monthly viral load per guideline.
